items.stem: Ms. Rivera was praised for her ___ handling of the client's complaint.
items.expl: Before the noun handling, we need an adjective: professional.

items.stem: The new software allows employees to work more ___.
items.expl: The word describes the verb work, so we need an adverb: efficiently.

items.stem: All visitors must show proper ___ at the front desk.
items.expl: After the adjective proper, we need a noun: identification.

items.stem: The marketing team has ___ improved the company's online presence.
items.expl: Between has and the past participle, we need an adverb: significantly.

items.stem: Our hotel is ___ located near the airport and the city center.
items.expl: The word describes the participle located, so we need an adverb: conveniently.

items.stem: The director expressed her ___ to all the volunteers.
items.expl: After her, we need a noun: appreciation.

items.stem: Please read the safety instructions ___ before using the machine.
items.expl: The word describes the verb read, so we need an adverb: carefully.

items.stem: The training session was so ___ that many staff asked for another one.
items.expl: So + adjective + that: informative.

items.stem: Mr. Ito is ___ for checking all invoices before payment.
items.expl: Be responsible for means 'have the job of'.

items.stem: The company's ___ to quality has earned it many loyal customers.
items.expl: After company's, we need a noun: commitment.

items.stem: Applicants should have ___ communication skills.
items.expl: Before the noun communication skills, we need an adjective: excellent.

items.stem: The sales figures were ___ higher than last year.
items.expl: The word describes the comparative higher, so we need an adverb: considerably.

items.stem: We are ___ to announce the opening of our new branch.
items.expl: Be pleased to + verb means 'be happy to'.

items.stem: The museum offers free ___ on the first Sunday of every month.
items.expl: After the adjective free, we need a noun: admission.

items.stem: Our technicians will respond ___ to any service request.
items.expl: The word describes the verb respond, so we need an adverb: promptly.

items.stem: The proposal was rejected because it was not financially ___.
items.expl: After be and the adverb financially, we need an adjective: feasible.

items.stem: Ms. Garcia is one of the most ___ designers in the company.
items.expl: The most + adjective + noun: creative.

items.stem: The ___ of the new factory will create 500 jobs.
items.expl: The … of needs a noun: construction.

items.stem: Employees must complete the form ___ and return it to HR.
items.expl: The word describes the verb complete, so we need an adverb: accurately.

items.stem: The CEO gave a very ___ speech at the annual dinner.
items.expl: The speech gave people inspiration, so we use the -ing adjective: inspiring.

items.stem: We were ___ by the high quality of the samples.
items.expl: We describes people's feelings, so we use the -ed adjective: impressed.

items.stem: The new parking rules will become ___ on July 1.
items.expl: Become effective means 'start to apply'.

items.stem: The board of directors ___ the merger at next week's meeting.
items.expl: Next week is in the future: will discuss.

items.stem: Since joining the company, Mr. Ahmed ___ three major projects.
items.expl: Since + a starting point shows a period up to now: has managed.

items.stem: The package ___ to the wrong address yesterday.
items.expl: Yesterday + passive: was sent.

items.stem: Currently, our engineers ___ a new mobile application.
items.expl: Currently signals the present continuous.

items.stem: The conference room ___ for the training session tomorrow.
items.expl: The room receives the action, and the booking is already done: has been reserved.

items.stem: By the end of this year, the company ___ 20 new stores.
items.expl: By the end of + a future time: future perfect, will have opened.

items.stem: Last quarter, profits ___ by nearly 10 percent.
items.expl: Last quarter is a finished past time: rise → rose.

items.stem: Ms. Lopez usually ___ the weekly sales report on Fridays.
items.expl: Usually + a singular subject: prepares.

items.stem: All orders ___ within two business days.
items.expl: Orders receive the action: are processed.

items.stem: When the fire alarm rang, the employees ___ a meeting.
items.expl: An action in progress that was interrupted uses the past continuous.

items.stem: The new policy ___ by the board last Monday.
items.expl: The policy receives the action, last Monday: was approved.

items.stem: Please make sure that the lights ___ off before you leave.
items.expl: The lights receive the action: are turned off.

items.stem: Mr. Park ___ for the company for over twenty years when he retired.
items.expl: Before a past moment (when he retired): past perfect.

items.stem: If sales ___ to grow, we will hire more staff.
items.expl: First conditional: If + present simple.

items.stem: The quarterly meeting will be held ___ the third floor.
items.expl: Floors take on: on the third floor.

items.stem: Payment is due ___ receipt of the invoice.
items.expl: Upon receipt means 'as soon as it is received'.

items.stem: The store will be closed ___ the holiday period.
items.expl: Throughout + a period means 'for the whole of it'.

items.stem: Ms. Lee has worked in sales ___ 2015.
items.expl: A starting point in time: since.

items.stem: The report must be submitted ___ Friday at 5 p.m.
items.expl: By means 'not later than' for a deadline.

items.stem: The bus stop is located directly ___ the hotel entrance.
items.expl: Opposite means 'facing, on the other side'.

items.stem: The museum is open daily ___ 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.
items.expl: From … to … shows a time range.

items.stem: Refunds will be issued ___ 14 days of the return.
items.expl: Within + a period means 'inside that time'.

items.stem: The training is mandatory for all staff, ___ managers.
items.expl: Including works as a preposition: it adds part of a group.

items.stem: The meeting was postponed ___ the director's illness.
items.expl: The director's illness is a noun phrase: because of.

items.stem: The lecture was interesting, ___ a bit too long.
items.expl: Albeit means 'although' and is followed by an adjective or phrase. It is formal.

items.stem: Customers can pay ___ cash or by credit card.
items.expl: Pay in cash, but pay by card.

items.stem: Ms. Clark is responsible ___ training new employees.
items.expl: Responsible for + noun or -ing.

items.stem: The price of the tour includes meals and accommodation, but not ___ insurance.
items.expl: Travel insurance is a compound noun.

items.stem: We apologize ___ any inconvenience this may cause.
items.expl: Apologise for something.

items.stem: Please reply ___ this email by Thursday.
items.expl: Reply to something.

items.stem: ___ the weather was bad, the outdoor concert went ahead as planned.
items.expl: A clause with a contrasting meaning: Although.

items.stem: You will not be able to enter the building ___ you show your ID card.
items.expl: Unless means 'if not'.

items.stem: Ms. Brown will lead the meeting ___ Mr. Davis is on vacation.
items.expl: Mr. Davis is on vacation is a clause: while.

items.stem: Both the manager ___ her assistant attended the conference.
items.expl: Both … and.

items.stem: Please arrive early ___ we can start the meeting on time.
items.expl: So that shows purpose.

items.stem: Neither the printer ___ the scanner is working today.
items.expl: Neither … nor.

items.stem: The shop offers free delivery ___ the order is over $50.
items.expl: A condition: if.

items.stem: ___ submitting the form, check that all information is correct.
items.expl: Before + -ing.

items.stem: The first design was simple, ___ the second one was more detailed.
items.expl: Whereas contrasts two clauses.

items.stem: ___ you have any questions, please contact our support team.
items.expl: A condition: If.

items.stem: The project was completed on time ___ several unexpected problems.
items.expl: Several unexpected problems is a noun phrase: in spite of.

items.stem: Not only did the hotel upgrade our room, ___ it also gave us free breakfast.
items.expl: Not only … but also.

items.stem: We will not start the meeting ___ everyone has arrived.
items.expl: Not … until means 'only when'.

items.stem: ___ the hotel nor the restaurant accepts credit cards.
items.expl: Neither … nor.

items.stem: Ms. Kim asked that all reports be sent directly to ___.
items.expl: After the preposition to, we need an object pronoun: her.

items.stem: The employees organized the farewell party by ___.
items.expl: By themselves means 'without help'.

items.stem: Mr. Chen forgot ___ laptop in the meeting room.
items.expl: Before the noun laptop, we need a possessive adjective: his.

items.stem: Our products are cheaper than ___ of our competitors.
items.expl: Those replaces a plural noun already mentioned (products).

items.stem: ___ who wish to join the tour should sign up at the front desk.
items.expl: Those who means 'the people who'.

items.stem: The company celebrated ___ 50th anniversary last month.
items.expl: The company is singular, so the possessive is its. It's means it is.

items.stem: The guests said they enjoyed ___ stay at our hotel.
items.expl: Before the noun stay, we need a possessive adjective: their.

items.stem: Mr. Diaz prefers to review the contracts ___ before signing them.
items.expl: Himself emphasises that he does it personally.

items.stem: Please ___ the attached file for the meeting agenda.
items.expl: Refer to means 'look at for information'.

items.stem: The hotel offers a free airport ___ service for all guests.
items.expl: An airport shuttle is a bus or car that takes guests to and from the airport.

items.stem: Due to high ___, the new phone sold out in two days.
items.expl: High demand means many people want to buy it.

items.stem: All employees must ___ the new safety regulations.
items.expl: Comply with rules means 'obey them'.

items.stem: The company will ___ all travel expenses for the conference.
items.expl: Reimburse expenses means 'pay back money someone has spent'.

items.stem: The job ___ was posted on the company website last week.
items.expl: A job opening is a position that needs to be filled.

items.stem: We need to ___ the deadline because the materials arrived late.
items.expl: Extend a deadline means 'give more time'.

items.stem: The warranty ___ all repairs for two years.
items.expl: A warranty covers repairs: it includes them.

items.stem: Ms. Ortiz was ___ to regional manager after five years.
items.expl: Be promoted to means 'be given a higher position'.

items.stem: Our customer service team is ___ 24 hours a day.
items.expl: Available means 'ready to help or be used'.

items.stem: Please ___ a table for six at 7 p.m.
items.expl: Reserve a table means 'book it in advance'.

items.stem: The flight was ___ because of heavy fog.
items.expl: A delayed flight leaves later than planned.

items.stem: The manager asked us to ___ our ideas at the next meeting.
items.expl: Ask somebody to + base verb: present.

items.stem: To ___ for the discount, customers must spend at least $50.
items.expl: Qualify for means 'meet the conditions to get'.

items.stem: The new manager quickly ___ a good relationship with her team.
items.expl: Establish a relationship means 'build it'.

items.stem: Interested candidates should ___ their résumés by email.
items.expl: Submit a résumé means 'send it officially'.

items.stem: The factory is running at full ___ to meet the holiday orders.
items.expl: At full capacity means 'producing as much as possible'.

items.stem: We will ___ you as soon as your order is ready.
items.expl: Notify somebody means 'tell them officially'.

items.stem: Please keep your receipt as ___ of purchase.
items.expl: Proof of purchase shows that you bought something.

items.stem: The company plans to ___ its business into three new markets.
items.expl: Expand into new markets means 'grow into them'.

items.stem: Staff are ___ to wear their ID badges at all times.
items.expl: Be required to means 'must'.

items.stem: The concert was canceled, and all ticket holders will receive a full ___.
items.expl: A refund is money paid back.

items.stem: Our sales ___ have increased by 20 percent.
items.expl: Sales figures are the numbers that show sales.

items.stem: The hotel was fully ___, so we had to stay somewhere else.
items.expl: Fully booked means there are no free rooms.

items.stem: The two companies have agreed to ___ on the new project.
items.expl: Collaborate on means 'work together on'.

items.stem: The CEO will ___ the opening speech at the conference.
items.expl: Deliver a speech means 'give a speech'.

items.stem: Please ___ from smoking inside the building.
items.expl: Refrain from + -ing means 'do not do'. It is formal.

items.stem: The bank will ___ a fee for international transfers.
items.expl: Charge a fee means 'ask for money for a service'.

items.stem: This year's conference attracted ___ participants than last year's.
items.expl: Comparative + than: more participants.

items.stem: This is the ___ sales result in the company's history.
items.expl: The + superlative: the best.

items.stem: The new model is ___ lighter than the old one.
items.expl: Much makes a comparative stronger: much lighter. Very cannot go before a comparative.

items.stem: ___ employee will receive a bonus this year.
items.expl: Every + singular noun: every employee.

items.stem: There were ___ complaints about the new menu.
items.expl: Complaints is countable, so we use few.

items.stem: The candidate ___ we interviewed yesterday has accepted the offer.
items.expl: The person is the object of interviewed: whom (or who, that).

items.stem: The building ___ the conference will be held has a large parking lot.
items.expl: For a place (= in which): where.

items.stem: Thank you for ___ our survey.
items.expl: After a preposition (for), use -ing.

items.stem: We look forward to ___ with you again.
items.expl: Look forward to + -ing.

items.stem: The manager decided ___ the event until next month.
items.expl: Decide + to + verb.

items.stem: Customers who wish ___ their orders should call before noon.
items.expl: Wish + to + verb.

items.stem: ___ the end of the year, all employees will receive a gift card.
items.expl: At the end of a period.

items.stem: The marketing manager, ___ ideas helped increase sales, will speak first.
items.expl: Whose shows possession: the manager's ideas.

items.stem: Please inform us ___ any changes to your address.
items.expl: Inform somebody of something.

items.stem: The software update is ___ to fix the login problem.
items.expl: Be expected to means 'should happen, according to plans'.

items.stem: The accounting department will ___ the revised budget by Friday afternoon.
items.expl: After will, use the base-form verb circulate. The department will send the budget to the relevant staff.

items.stem: Employees are asked to keep their identification cards ___ at all times.
items.expl: Keep is followed by an object complement. Visible describes the cards' state, while the other choices are nouns or an adverb.

items.stem: The supplier promised to deliver the replacement parts ___ than expected.
items.expl: The word than calls for the comparative adverb sooner. The sentence compares the promised delivery time with the expected time.

items.stem: The customer service team has received several ___ about the delayed shipment.
items.expl: Several must modify a plural countable noun. Complaints fits the meaning and the grammar; the other forms are verb forms.

items.stem: Please submit the travel request ___ you book the hotel.
items.expl: Before introduces the earlier action. Employees should submit the request first and book the hotel afterward.

items.stem: The new printer is capable ___ producing color brochures.
items.expl: Capable is followed by the preposition of and a gerund. Producing completes the phrase capable of producing.

items.stem: Ms. Patel will attend the conference ___ her supervisor is unavailable.
items.expl: Because introduces a complete reason clause: her supervisor is unavailable. During and despite require a noun phrase instead.

items.stem: The maintenance crew ___ the air-conditioning system before the store opened.
items.expl: The inspection happened before the past event of the store opening, so the past perfect had inspected is appropriate.

items.stem: Customers who register online will receive a ___ confirmation email.
items.expl: An adjective is needed before the noun phrase confirmation email. Detailed describes the information in the message.

items.stem: The board approved the proposal ___ several members had raised concerns.
items.expl: Although connects two contrasting clauses. The board approved the proposal even though some members had concerns.

items.stem: All invoices must be checked ___ payment is authorized.
items.expl: Before introduces the later event, authorization. The invoices must be checked first.

items.stem: The company is seeking an applicant with experience ___ international clients.
items.expl: Experience is followed naturally by a gerund when describing an activity. Serving international clients is the required experience.

items.stem: The manager asked the receptionist to reserve a room for ___.
items.expl: The preposition for needs an object pronoun. Us is the object form of we; our and ours are possessive forms.

items.stem: The warranty covers repairs that result ___ manufacturing defects.
items.expl: Result from means be caused by. Manufacturing defects are the cause of the repairs covered by the warranty.

items.stem: The marketing report provides a ___ comparison of the two campaigns.
items.expl: The blank modifies the noun comparison, so an adjective is required. Useful describes the comparison.

items.stem: If the parts arrive today, the technician ___ the machine tomorrow.
items.expl: This is a first conditional: present simple after if and will plus the base verb in the result clause.

items.stem: The conference organizers sent the schedule to all ___ participants.
items.expl: Registered is a past participle used as an adjective meaning participants who have completed registration.

items.stem: The office will remain closed ___ the electrical work is completed.
items.expl: Until marks the endpoint of the closure. The office remains closed up to the time the work is completed.

items.stem: The director spoke ___ about the need to protect customer data.
items.expl: An adverb is needed to modify spoke. Seriously describes the director's manner of speaking.

items.stem: The delivery driver could not enter the building ___ he had a valid access code.
items.expl: Although introduces a contrast between having a valid code and being unable to enter. Because of would need a noun phrase.

items.stem: Please keep a copy of the receipt ___ you need to request a refund.
items.expl: In case introduces a possible future situation for which the receipt may be needed.

items.stem: The warehouse has enough space to store the equipment ___ the renovation.
items.expl: During is a preposition followed by a noun phrase. It identifies the period when the equipment will be stored.

items.stem: The training manual is available in both printed and digital ___.
items.expl: The phrase lists two types of the manual, so the plural noun formats is required.

items.stem: The hotel offers guests a ___ breakfast before the early flight.
items.expl: Complimentary means provided free of charge, which fits the hotel breakfast. Compliment is a different noun meaning praise.

items.stem: The sales representative will contact you as soon as she ___ the updated figures.
items.expl: In a future time clause after as soon as, use the present simple receives rather than will receive.

items.stem: The audit revealed that the records had been stored ___.
items.expl: The adverb improperly modifies had been stored and means not in the correct way.

items.stem: The supplier offered a discount ___ we placed a larger order.
items.expl: Provided that introduces the condition for receiving the discount. The other choices do not express a condition here.

items.stem: The employee handbook explains how staff should respond ___ emergencies.
items.expl: Respond to is the fixed collocation. Emergencies are what staff must respond to.

items.stem: The project was completed on time, ___ the limited budget.
items.expl: Despite is followed by a noun phrase and expresses contrast: the project succeeded even with a limited budget.

items.stem: The company plans to expand its customer support team ___ next year.
items.expl: The blank modifies the verb expand, so the adverb significantly is needed.

items.stem: Applicants should attach a résumé ___ their application form.
items.expl: The verb attach takes the preposition to before the item receiving the attachment: attach a résumé to the form.

items.stem: The procurement officer requested three ___ from different suppliers.
items.expl: Three requires a plural countable noun. Quotations are written offers stating a price.

items.stem: The receptionist will notify visitors when their host ___.
items.expl: Host is singular, so the present simple form is arrives. A future time clause uses present simple rather than will.

items.stem: The company reduced shipping costs by negotiating a more favorable ___.
items.expl: The article a and adjective favorable require a singular noun. Contract names the agreement being negotiated.

items.stem: Please ensure that the package is labeled ___.
items.expl: The adverb correctly modifies is labeled and describes how the package should be labeled.

items.stem: The new policy applies to all employees, ___ their job title.
items.expl: Regardless of is followed by a noun phrase and means that the policy applies without considering job title.

items.stem: The flight was delayed ___ heavy fog at the airport.
items.expl: Because of introduces a noun phrase that gives the reason for the delay.

items.stem: The design team is expected ___ the first draft by Monday.
items.expl: The passive expression be expected is followed by an infinitive: to finish the draft.

items.stem: The director asked whether the figures were ___ enough to publish.
items.expl: The linking verb were requires an adjective. Reliable describes figures that can be trusted.

items.stem: The café will close early today ___ a private event.
items.expl: For introduces the reason for closing early. It is followed by the noun phrase a private event.

items.stem: The software update includes several security ___ for mobile users.
items.expl: Several requires a plural noun. Improvements names the security changes included in the update.

items.stem: The courier delivered the documents ___ than the client had expected.
items.expl: Than requires the comparative adverb earlier. The delivery happened before the client's expectation.

items.stem: The committee will meet to discuss ___ the proposal should be revised.
items.expl: Whether introduces an indirect yes-or-no question after discuss. The committee will consider if revision is needed.

items.stem: Our representatives are available to answer questions ___ the product demonstration.
items.expl: After is followed by the noun phrase the product demonstration and identifies when representatives are available.

items.stem: The office manager reminded staff ___ the new visitor procedure.
items.expl: Remind someone of something is the fixed construction. The staff were reminded of the procedure.

items.stem: The hotel requires guests to provide a credit card ___ check-in.
items.expl: At is used with a specific event or point in time: at check-in.

items.stem: The report was praised for its ___ analysis of customer behavior.
items.expl: An adjective is required before analysis. Thorough means complete and careful.

items.stem: The sales figures have increased steadily ___ the new campaign began.
items.expl: Since introduces the starting point of a continuing change: the campaign began.

items.stem: The company hired a consultant to improve its online ___.
items.expl: Online presence is the standard noun phrase for how visible an organization is online.

items.stem: The technician found the instructions too ___ to follow.
items.expl: Confusing describes something that causes confusion. The instructions cause the difficulty, so confusing is correct.

items.stem: The museum's opening hours may change ___ public holidays.
items.expl: On is used with days and named occasions. Public holidays are the occasions when the hours may change.

items.stem: Please keep the doors closed so that the air-conditioning system can operate ___.
items.expl: An adverb modifies operate. Efficiently explains how the air-conditioning system can operate.

items.stem: The supplier will replace any items that arrive ___.
items.expl: Damaged is a past participle adjective describing items that arrive in a damaged condition.

items.stem: The manager approved the request, ___ it exceeded the original budget.
items.expl: Even though introduces a complete contrasting clause. The request was approved despite exceeding the budget.

items.stem: The conference room is reserved ___ the afternoon session.
items.expl: The room is reserved for the session, so for introduces the intended use.

items.stem: The brochure gives a ___ description of the tour itinerary.
items.expl: A noun is modified by an adjective. Brief describes the short description in the brochure.

items.stem: The manager will review the schedule and make ___ changes if necessary.
items.expl: Any is used before the plural count noun changes in this conditional sentence.

items.stem: The restaurant has expanded its menu to include more vegetarian ___.
items.expl: More modifies a plural count noun here. Vegetarian options are choices for customers who do not eat meat.

items.stem: The employee handbook should be read carefully before it is ___ to new staff.
items.expl: The handbook receives the action, so the passive form is distributed after is.

items.stem: The airline apologized ___ the cancellation and offered a refund.
items.expl: Apologize for is the fixed phrase used before the problem being apologized for.

items.stem: The new filing system makes documents much easier ___.
items.expl: The pattern is make something easier to do. To locate completes the adjective phrase easier to locate.

items.stem: The manager asked for a more ___ explanation of the price increase.
items.expl: More modifies the adjective specific, which describes the requested explanation.

items.stem: The shipment cannot be released until the customs forms ___.
items.expl: The forms receive the action, so are completed is passive. A time clause after until uses present simple.

items.stem: The human resources department will conduct a ___ survey next month.
items.expl: An adjective is needed before survey. Confidential describes information kept private.

items.stem: New employees must complete the safety course ___ their first week.
items.expl: Within introduces a period containing the deadline: during the first week.

items.stem: The operations team is responsible for ___ daily inventory levels.
items.expl: Responsible for is followed by a gerund. Monitoring describes the team's regular duty.

items.stem: The candidate's references were contacted to verify her professional ___.
items.expl: Professional modifies the noun experience, which means the candidate's work background.

items.stem: The factory will stop production ___ the inspection is complete.
items.expl: Until marks the point when production can resume. The inspection is a complete clause after it.

items.stem: The supervisor gave the team clear instructions, and everyone followed ___ carefully.
items.expl: Followed needs an object pronoun. Them refers back to the instructions.

items.stem: The updated schedule is ___ on the company intranet.
items.expl: The linking verb is requires an adjective. Available means the schedule can be accessed.

items.stem: The factory installed new lights to improve visibility and reduce energy ___.
items.expl: Energy consumption is the noun phrase for the amount of energy used.

items.stem: The supervisor will approve the overtime request once the project manager ___.
items.expl: Project manager is singular, and a future time clause after once uses present simple agrees.

items.stem: The company is looking for a candidate who can work ___ under pressure.
items.expl: Effectively is an adverb modifying work and describes performance under pressure.

items.stem: The equipment must be handled with ___ to avoid damage.
items.expl: With care is the noun phrase meaning carefully. The preposition with is followed by the noun care.

items.stem: The manager was pleased ___ the team's progress during the trial period.
items.expl: Pleased with is the fixed expression for being satisfied with something.

items.stem: The new employee handbook contains useful information about workplace ___.
items.expl: Workplace conduct is the noun phrase for behavior at work. The other forms do not fit after workplace.

items.stem: The manager requested that all visitors ___ their badges at the entrance.
items.expl: After requested that in a formal requirement, use the base form wear for the subjunctive.

items.stem: The new packaging is designed to be both attractive and ___.
items.expl: Both ... and joins parallel adjectives. Durable describes packaging that lasts a long time.

items.stem: The company will offer a bonus to employees who ___ the training by June.
items.expl: The relative clause describes a future condition, so it uses present simple complete rather than will complete.

items.stem: The repair should take no ___ than two hours.
items.expl: No more than means not exceeding a limit. More is the comparative form required before than.

items.stem: The company has made a significant ___ in reducing paper waste.
items.expl: The article a and adjective significant require a singular noun. Improvement means progress.

items.stem: The loading area is accessible only ___ authorized personnel.
items.expl: Accessible to is the fixed phrase. Authorized personnel are the people permitted to enter.

items.stem: The company postponed the launch ___ a shortage of components.
items.expl: Due to introduces the noun phrase that explains the reason for postponing the launch.

items.stem: The assistant prepared the meeting room ___ and checked the projector.
items.expl: In advance is the adverbial phrase meaning before the event. It modifies prepared.

items.stem: The employee was promoted because of her ___ performance.
items.expl: An adjective is needed before performance. Outstanding means exceptionally good.

items.stem: The instructions are written clearly enough for users to follow them ___.
items.expl: Independently is an adverb modifying follow and means without assistance.

items.stem: The company will not issue a refund unless the product ___ within thirty days.
items.expl: The product receives the action, so the passive is is returned. Unless clauses use present simple for a future condition.

items.stem: The training coordinator sent a reminder to everyone who had not ___ yet.
items.expl: Had not is followed by a past participle. Registered means the people had not completed registration.

items.stem: The warehouse uses a barcode system in order to process orders more ___.
items.expl: Rapidly is an adverb modifying process. It explains that orders are handled at greater speed.

items.stem: The committee agreed to meet again ___ the proposal needs further discussion.
items.expl: If introduces the condition for meeting again: the proposal may need more discussion.

items.stem: The company provides employees ___ protective equipment at no charge.
items.expl: Provide someone with something is the fixed construction. Employees receive protective equipment.

items.stem: The new system is expected to make data entry less ___.
items.expl: Less modifies an adjective. Time-consuming describes a task that takes a lot of time.

items.stem: The supervisor praised the workers for completing the task ___.
items.expl: Ahead of schedule is the standard phrase meaning before the planned time.

items.stem: The report must be signed by a manager before it can be sent ___.
items.expl: Externally is the adverb modifying sent and means to outside recipients.

items.stem: The bank will waive the monthly fee for customers who maintain a ___ balance.
items.expl: An adjective is required before balance. Minimum describes the lowest required amount.

items.stem: The cashier counted the money twice to ensure that the amount was ___.
items.expl: The linking verb was takes an adjective. Accurate describes an amount that is correct.

items.stem: The company offers customers several convenient payment ___.
items.expl: Several requires a plural countable noun. Methods are different ways to pay.

items.stem: The invoice includes a charge ___ late payment.
items.expl: Charge for is the correct collocation for a fee connected with late payment.

items.stem: The accountant noticed that one receipt was missing from the expense ___.
items.expl: Expense report is the standard noun phrase for a record of spending.
